name: EPA ECHO sewer overflow and bypass event reports (eRule Phase 2, NeT-SewerOverflow), NE rows
operator: US EPA (ECHO); reports filed by permittees through NeT-SewerOverflow
waters_covered: statewide; receiving water free text in a child table (often blank)
access_detail: Daily ZIP from ECHO; table sewer_overflow_bypass_report_events.csv joined to sewer_overflow_bypass_receiving_waters.csv on sewer_overflow_bypass_event_key; filter permit_identifier prefix. Pipeline already has pipeline/ingest/echo_sewer_overflow_events.py. Trimmed sample in raw/sobe-sample.json.
cadence: Extract rebuilt daily; these are the 5-day written reports, so they appear days to weeks after the event (start-to-receipt median 23 days; 10% within 1 day, 10% over 83 days).
history: Rows from April 2023 (NeT pilot) to date
license: EPA public data; no restriction stated
legal_basis: 40 CFR 127 (NPDES eRule Phase 2, from 2025-12-21); 40 CFR 122.41(l)(6) five-day written report
status_reason: The only dated, statewide, machine-readable overflow feed for Nebraska, read by the national eRule ingester (echo-sewer-overflow) with Nebraska in its states. 2026-11-04 extract: 162 current NE rows from 21 permits (CSO 89, SSO 64, BYP 9), starts 2022-04-15 to 2026-10-06; every row with a point, 158 with a volume, 49 with a receiving-water row. 51 kept from 13 permits; 111 dropped (83 building backups, 28 SSOs and manhole CSOs naming no water and no water impact). Received a median 22.5 days after the start (10% within a day, 10% 83 days or more). Times read in the zone of the event's own point (Mountain in the eighteen counties and the western part of Cherry County that 49 CFR 71.7(c) puts west of the boundary, Central elsewhere): all 162 points lie in the Central part.

name: Nebraska DWEE Beach Watch: MonitoredBeachAlert (ArcGIS)
operator: Nebraska Department of Water, Energy, and Environment (formerly NDEE)
access_detail: Query .../MonitoredBeachAlertNDEE/FeatureServer/0/query?where=1%3D1&outFields=*&f=json (public). Backs the BeachWatch Experience f32c1c97d3f242d09ec6c9ddfb0f1547 (web map 035e8af5d80d4fbdaf045656f75202aa). The Beach Watch page deq-iis.ne.gov/zs/bw/ returned 503/reset when checked. Sample in raw/beachwatch-alert-sample.json.

sample_record.HealthDescription: This beach is under health alert

cannot_fill: ended_at (alert lift is implicit in next week's row)
cadence: Samples Mondays, posted Fridays (map refresh at midnight Friday), mid-May to mid-September
history: 2026 season in the layer (earlier seasons not checked)
license: No licence statement on the service
status_reason: Read through the generic ArcGIS reader (ne-dwee-beachwatch). Public layer with every weekly beach sample of the 2026 season (1,022 rows at 57 beaches, sample weeks 20 to 37, 2026-05-18 to 2026-09-14, fetched 2026-11-07): station, lat/long, sample date, E. coli, microcystin, HealthAlert YES/NO and description. 20 rows on health alert (microcystin above 8 ug/L: Rockford Lake, Maskenthine Reservoir, Cub Creek Lake, Big Indian Lake, Iron Horse Trail Lake, Kirkman's Cove Lake, Maple Creek Recreation Area Lake) read as the agency's bloom advisories; 38 rows labelled 'Elevated health risk for E. coli' (above 235/100 mL), for which DWEE issues no advisory, read as a caution; 57 records.
notes: Health alerts also announced by joint DWEE/Game and Parks/DHHS press releases, a Beach Watch listserv and social media.

name: Nebraska Beach Watch page
status_reason: 503 to WebFetch and connection reset to curl on 2026-11-03; described in DWEE release dwee.nebraska.gov/node/4996 (fetched).

name: DWEE guide: Creating Event Report in NeTSSO
status_reason: Confirms Nebraska permittees file sewer overflow and bypass reports in EPA's NeT-SewerOverflow (hence the SOBE rows).

name: Title 126 Chapter 18 (proposed Chapter 1) release notification
status_reason: Oil and hazardous substance releases (notice within 15 minutes; 2026 proposal allows up to 24 hours); does not address sewage.

status_reason: Omaha Public Works announces large overflows through media with a map of the affected stretch (Boxelder and West Papillion creeks, 2026-10-02: 'not to touch the water'). No city web notice found.

status_reason: Only features 102 and 205R report DMRs, including 'Number of Events', 'Duration of discharge' and 'Flow, total' (likely the treated outfalls); the 25 CSO outfalls have no monthly counts.
